email.subject: Urgent: CHF 2,450.00 is being moved out of your account

body.v: We have stopped a transfer of CHF 2,450.00 from your account to a recipient we do not recognise. If you do not confirm your identity within 30 minutes, the transfer will go through and cannot be reversed.
For your security, please do not ignore this message.

hotspots.explain: The address ends in swissalpbank-alerts.example, not the bank's real domain swissalpbank.example. Anyone can register a name that looks close.
"Dear customer": your real bank knows your name and uses it.
A large amount and the word "Urgent" in the subject are there to make you panic before you think.
A 30-minute deadline leaves you no time to check. Your real bank gives you time and other ways to reach it.
The button says "Stop the transfer now", but it leads to swissalpbank-secure-login.example, a different domain that only looks like the bank's.
A signature is easy to copy. It is not a red flag by itself, but it proves nothing either.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone pretending to be SwissAlpBank. The name says SwissAlpBank, but the address is on swissalpbank-alerts.example, which is not the bank's domain.
choices: SwissAlpBank, because the name says so
Someone using an address that only looks like the bank's
Your personal adviser at the bank
cues: Compare the sender address with swissalpbank.example.
A display name can be set to anything.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Fear and hurry: a large sum of money is about to leave your account and you only have 30 minutes.
choices: Fear of losing money, with a rush to act
None: it is a calm routine notice

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Click the link and log in, which would hand your login details to whoever wrote the email.
choices: Click a link and log in
Call the number on the back of your card
Nothing: it is only for information
cues: What does the button lead to?

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the SwissAlpBank app, or type the bank's address yourself, and look at your recent transactions.
choices: Click the link to see whether it is real
Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and check your account
Reply to the email and ask whether it is genuine
cues: A channel you control is one you open yourself, not one the email gives you.

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and check your recent transactions
actions.consequence: No transfer is listed. The email was fake and you gave nothing away.

actions.label: Click "Stop the transfer now" and log in
actions.consequence: The page looks like your bank, but your login details go straight to the scammer, who can now get into your account.

actions.label: Reply and ask whether the email is genuine
actions.consequence: The scammer answers that it is genuine and pushes you again. Your reply also tells them your address is in use.

actions.label: Report the email as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: Good call. Nothing was clicked and your mail provider learns to catch similar emails.

attacker_reveal: I copied the bank's name, picked an address that looks close enough and invented a payment to scare you. The 30-minute deadline was there so you would click before checking. If you had logged in on my page, I would have your password.
